answer: In an agent economy, each participant must undertake a unique voyage across a computational reef of cryptographic puzzles arranged in a trellis structure. To register, an agent solves sequential challenges where each node depends on prior outputs and a personal key, making mass Sybil creation prohibitively expensive because the attacker must expend fresh compute for every fake identity without reuse of solutions. This binds reputation to non-transferable work, raising the cost of flooding the system far above the benefit of any single colluding cluster.
